newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bakrie denies report on Freeport.
newsitem.headline: Bakrie denies report on Freeport.

text.p: Indonesia's diversified holding company Bakrie Brothers denied on Friday a local media report quoting rumours as saying it planned to sell its stake in PT Freeport Indonesia.
"The news is not true. So far Bakrie does not have any intention to sell our stake in Indocopper Investama," Bakrie's group public relations told Reuters.

He said the group still held a 49 percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama, which has a 9.36 percent stake in PT Freeport Indonesia, operator of one of the world's biggest copper and gold mines in Irian Jaya province.
The economic tabloid Kontan on Friday reported rumours that Bakrie Brothers might sell it stake in PT Indocopper Investama to the Indonesia government.
PT Indocopper Investama, the Indonesian government and the U.S. Freeport McMoran Copper and Gold Inc control 9.36 percent, 9.36 percent and 81.28 percent respectively of PT Freeport Indonesia.
In the late trading on Friday, Bakrie Brothers was unchanged at 950 rupiah on a volume of 418,500 shares on the Jakarta stock exchange.
Bakrie Brother is engaged in telecommunications services, in trading and manufacturing construction materials and in investment activities. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
